newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain consumer confidence hits peak in Q1 in poll.
newsitem.headline: Spain consumer confidence hits peak in Q1 in poll.

text.p: Spanish consumer confidence reached a six-year peak in the first quarter, according to a survey published on Monday by the financial newspaper Expansion.
In the first quarter of 1997, the Consumer confidence Index (ICC) rose to an average of less 12 points, the highest level since the first six months of 1991, the paper reported today.

The best ever rating in the quarterly survey El Termometro, carried out by Intergallup, was registered in the third quarter of 1989 at plus 13 points, while the worst was in the fourth quarter of 1993 at minus 68 points.
During the last quarter of 1996, ICC was at minus 34, while it was at less than 30 points in the first quarter of 1996.

Expansion added that behind the improvement in consumer confidence, was economic growth, a fall in inflation below the three percent requirement, and the prospective entry in the European Monetary Union.
The breakdown for the first quarter of 1997 shows that ICC hit a record in January at minus six points, falling to minus 17 points in February and rising again to minus 14 points in March.
Two different polls published on Sunday showed that nearly one year after taking power, Spain's Popular Party government won solid marks for its economic policies.
